title: Thinner Than 1 mm? Least Count Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A ruler, a kitchen scale and a stopwatch each have a smallest step. So can a ruler measure a bicycle spoke that is thinner than its smallest mark? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn the least count of measuring instruments.

You will watch a vernier callipers close on a spoke on a live measuring bench, with the reading, the matching vernier mark and a graph of reading vs jaw opening updating together. We derive the vernier least count step by step (10 VSD = 9 MSD, so LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = 0.1 mm), then turn a screw gauge one full circle to see why its least count is pitch / number of circular divisions = 0.01 mm. Two pause-and-think checks compare ruler vs vernier and vernier vs screw gauge. Then a worked screw gauge reading, the exam trap about 1/N, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
